clue.text: He sees the benefit of great works

definitions.text: He sees the benefit of great works

parts.words: He sees the benefit of great works
parts.note: great works suggests artistic masterpieces, but here works are factories, and the person profiting from them is a factory owner

explanation.surface: A connoisseur appreciating the value of great art.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory owner profits from large manufacturing plants, which are called works.

clue.text: Caught in gentle frolicking and forgetfulness

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for caught sits inside the rearranged letters
letters frolicking around are playing about out of order, so the word gentle is rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone caught up in light-hearted play forgets everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frolicking' makes NEGLET from gentle, and 'in' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Neglect is a failure to attend to something, a kind of careless omission or forgetting.

clue.text: Fruit, nothing like a peach, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same but is spelt differently

parts.note: a peach is a beauty, so something nothing like one is unattractive, ugly

explanation.surface: A fruit that, by sound, is no beauty, unlike a peach.
explanation.walkthrough: A peach in British slang is a lovely person, so the opposite is ugly.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a tangelo with wrinkled, lumpy skin.

clue.text: Move to continue playing football, or concede defeat

definitions.meaning: in soccer, when the ball goes out over the touchline a player hurls it back onto the pitch to restart
to give up, as in throwing in the towel or one's cards

explanation.surface: A footballer must choose between restarting play or giving up.
explanation.definitionFit: The restart move in soccer and the phrasal verb for surrendering share the same two words.

clue.text: Concentrated on treating tennis elbow initially

indicators.note: treating suggests processing or working the letters over, so they are rearranged
initially picks the opening letter of the word elbow

explanation.surface: A focused doctor working on a patient's tennis elbow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treating' rearranges TENNIS plus E, the first letter of elbow ('initially').
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means strong and focused, as in concentrated effort or flavour.

clue.text: Gracious, that's an uncommon chap

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of surprise, as in good gracious or good heavens
uncommon here means not a commoner: a peer of the realm, a nobleman

explanation.surface: Remarking in surprise that a man is unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncommon' reads as rare, but it means not one of the commons, i.e. a peer.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation of surprise and the title of a nobleman are the same word.

clue.text: Power at mains switches

indicators.note: switches means the letters swap places, so at mains is rearranged

explanation.surface: Electrical power controlled by switches on the mains supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switches' looks like electrical hardware but rearranges the letters of at mains.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, the strength to keep going.

clue.text: Stir food

parts.note: stir is slang for prison, and the traditional meagre diet of a prisoner is a plain loaf and a drink from the tap

explanation.surface: An instruction to mix a dish while cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' reads as a verb, but it is British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain rations of a loaf and a cup were the classic jail diet.

clue.text: Fail to cotton on

parts.note: to cotton on is to understand, and cotton suggests a strand of yarn, so failing to follow an argument becomes losing a strand

explanation.surface: Failing to grasp an idea.
explanation.walkthrough: The cotton of 'cotton on' doubles as yarn, the strand one loses.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to forget the line of a conversation or argument.

clue.text: Uniform for a soldier

definitions.meaning: uniform as an adjective, meaning even, steady, consistent
a professional soldier in a standing army, rather than a reservist

explanation.surface: Clothing issued to a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' reads as the noun for army dress, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means steady or even, and is also a full-time professional soldier.

clue.text: Storm ruined a party

parts.note: torn means ripped and spoilt, ruined
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Bad weather spoilt a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent rotating windstorm is a type of storm.

clue.text: Beaten by a single stroke

parts.note: in tennis a serve the opponent cannot touch wins the point with one stroke, and the receiver is said to have been so beaten

explanation.surface: Losing a contest by the narrowest margin, such as a single golf shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by a single stroke' suggests a narrow margin, but means beaten with one unreturnable serve.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis player is beaten by an unplayable serve, scoring the point in one shot.

clue.text: Double issue

parts.note: issue means offspring, so a pair of children born together is a double issue

explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' suggests a magazine edition, but here it means children.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a legal word for children, and two born at one birth are a pair.

clue.text: Penalty for striking

definitions.meaning: a sum of money paid as punishment
impressive and good-looking, as in a splendid view

explanation.surface: A punishment imposed on workers for going on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' suggests industrial action, but it is the adjective meaning impressive.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a monetary penalty and an adjective meaning handsome or excellent.

clue.text: Groups of mates

parts.note: team-mates form a side, and the word mates rearranged also spells the answer, a playful touch

explanation.walkthrough: Mates here are team-mates; the clue also plays on the letters of mates rearranging into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sides of players in a sport are made up of team-mates.

clue.text: Information about art form

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re means about or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: Details concerning a particular art form.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a category or style of art, such as a type of novel or music.

clue.text: His view of immortality led to his own mortality

definitions.text: His view of immortality led to his own mortality

parts.words: His view of immortality led to his own mortality
parts.note: in Greek myth a hunter glimpsed the goddess Artemis bathing; she turned him into a stag and his hounds killed him

explanation.walkthrough: 'view of immortality' reads as an opinion about living forever, but is a literal sight of an immortal goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical huntsman died after seeing the goddess Artemis naked, so a glimpse of a deity caused his death.

clue.text: This person gives a thrashing, one hears, and a pupil's under it

indicators.note: one hears signals that the phrase is spoken aloud, giving a different spelling

parts.note: this person is the setter, I, and gives a thrashing is lash, so together I LASH

explanation.surface: A teacher who beats pupils, sounding like an old-fashioned schoolmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupil' looks like a schoolchild beside 'thrashing', but it is the centre of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair fringing the eyelid sits above the dark centre of the eye.

clue.text: Bottles which don't split?

parts.note: empty bottles are jokingly called by this name, and split is slang for informing, as dead people tell no tales

explanation.walkthrough: 'split' reads as breaking glass but is slang for informing on someone; the dead tell no tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty wine or beer bottles are slangily named after corpses, which never betray secrets.

clue.text: One set off but got no place

definitions.text: One set off but got no place

parts.words: One set off but got no place
parts.note: in a horse race the starters who finish outside the first three get no place

explanation.walkthrough: 'got no place' sounds like getting nowhere, but means not finishing in the placings.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner who starts a race but finishes unplaced, and by extension any loser.

clue.text: All points identified chap as a journalist

parts.note: the four compass points are north, east, west and south, abbreviated N, E, W, S
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: Someone pointing out a man as a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter who gathers stories for papers or broadcasts is a journalist.

clue.text: Composer goes to court for judgment

parts.note: Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian opera composer

explanation.surface: A composer takes legal action and awaits the ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury's or judge's decision in a case is a judgment.

clue.text: Bad habit in which Tom gets dressed up as French aristocrat

indicators.note: in which says the rearranged name goes inside the word for a bad habit

parts.note: a vice is a bad habit

indicators.note: dressed up suggests rearranging or disguising, so the letters of Tom are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Tom with a bad habit of dressing up as a French noble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' suggests clothing beside 'dressed up', but means a vice; 'dressed up' signals the rearrangement and 'in which' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The French title equivalent to viscount is a rank of nobility.

clue.text: Reputation for enjoying poor health? Shame!

definitions.text: Reputation for enjoying poor health? Shame!

parts.words: Reputation for enjoying poor health? Shame!
parts.note: read literally, the phrase would be renown for sickness; in fact it means a bad name or disgrace

explanation.surface: Mock outrage at someone famous for being sickly.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase splits into ill plus fame, renown for sickness, while its real sense is disrepute.
explanation.definitionFit: The old phrase means disrepute, a bad reputation, as in a house of disgraceful kind.

clue.text: A footnote at end of service in part of church

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a note added at the foot of a letter

indicators.note: at end of picks the final letter of the word service

explanation.surface: A note added after a church service, in some part of the building.
explanation.definitionFit: The apse is the semicircular recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Now and again

parts.note: taken literally, the phrase means once now and once more again, so two times

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means occasionally, but read literally it counts two occasions.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done now and then done again has happened two times.

clue.text: Slight legato effect

definitions.meaning: a noun meaning an insult or aspersion
in music a curved line joining notes to be played smoothly

explanation.surface: A minor smooth effect in music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' reads as small, but is the noun meaning an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a disparaging remark and the notation linking notes played smoothly.

clue.text: Find love on the German river

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Discovering romance by a river in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a river of central Europe forming part of the German-Polish border.

clue.text: Famous ship with a right to set sail

parts.note: to go is to depart, as a ship does when it sets sail

explanation.surface: A famous vessel entitled to depart.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Jason and the Argonauts sailed in this ship to seek the Golden Fleece.

clue.text: A noble estate

parts.note: estate here is a rank or condition, so a noble one is the rank of a particular peer, or his lands

explanation.walkthrough: 'estate' suggests land, but also means rank, the dignity of an earl.
explanation.definitionFit: The title, rank or territory held by an earl is a noble estate.

clue.text: Sicilian port wine

definitions.meaning: a harbour town on the west coast of Sicily
a fortified dessert wine from that town

explanation.surface: A fortified wine from Sicily, like port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port wine' reads as one drink, but port is a harbour town here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian town gives its name to the fortified wine made there.

clue.text: Charm and wealth that buys one's way in

parts.note: to entrance is to charm or enchant
money is wealth

explanation.surface: Charisma and riches buy access to exclusive circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charm' reads as a noun but works as the verb entrance (stressed on the second syllable).
explanation.definitionFit: An admission fee is the sum paid to be let into a venue or club.
